passage:
Teacher's note, March.

While rechecking last term's science papers for the moderation meeting, I found that I had mis-added Vaibhav's total in November. He had asked me about it then and I had brushed him off. I called him in and said plainly that the mistake was mine and that his mark goes up. His eyebrows lifted and for a moment I saw a grin spread; I half expected a comment in front of his friends. Instead he said, "Thank you, ma'am. I'm glad it's fixed." Then he asked what he should have done to make sure I heard him earlier. We agreed he would bring a written query, and I would reply within the week.

Indu, Science teacher

qa.q: When did Indu find the mistake in Vaibhav's total?
qa.a: In March, while rechecking last term's papers for the moderation meeting.

qa.q: What did Indu notice about Vaibhav's feelings when she told him?
qa.a: A grin began to spread, so he felt vindicated, but he did not gloat. He thanked her and said he was glad it was fixed.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav and Indu agree to so that concerns are raised well in future?
qa.a: He will bring a written query and she will reply within the week.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav see the problem of not being heard in November?
qa.a: He seems to see it partly as something he can help fix, since he asked what he should have done to make sure she heard him earlier.

grounding: Months later a teacher admits a marking error; the student accepts it graciously and asks how to raise concerns better.

passage:
In March, Noor had asked Nilesh sir to recheck her history answer sheet. He'd refused. "My marking is final." She'd gone home and cried, then written down which answers she thought were wrong.
Now it was September. At the end of class, Nilesh sir called her to his desk. "Noor, I was going through the old sheets for the board sample. You were right about questions six and nine. I'm sorry. I've corrected your marks."
A hot rush of triumph went through her. She wanted to say, "I told you so." She pictured telling the whole class.
Instead, she took a breath. "Thank you, sir. That means a lot."
"You handled it well. Most people would have just fought."
Walking home through the Lucknow market, Noor smiled. She'd been right. But what she'd learned was also useful: write things down, stay calm, ask clearly. She'd do the same again.

qa.q: Which questions did Nilesh sir admit were wrongly marked?
How did Noor feel when Nilesh sir admitted the error?
qa.a: She felt a hot rush of triumph and vindication, and was tempted to gloat.

qa.q: Which choice did Noor make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She thanked him graciously instead of gloating, and kept the lesson of raising concerns calmly with written notes.

qa.q: How might Nilesh sir feel when admitting the mistake?
qa.a: He probably feels a little embarrassed but respects Noor for how calmly she handled it.

grounding: A teen whose teacher admits a marking error months later feels vindicated, resists gloating and accepts it graciously.

passage:
"Uma, stay back a minute."
"Yes, Thomas sir?"
"Remember the geography project in January? You said I'd missed your second map."
"I remember. You said I hadn't submitted it."
"I found it yesterday, stuck inside another student's folder. You had submitted it. I was wrong. I've updated your marks. I'm sorry."
Uma's heart jumped. For months she'd been angry. She'd even told her friends he never listened to anyone. She wanted to say, "Finally! I said so!"
She swallowed it. "Thank you, sir. I'm glad it's sorted."
"You kept your cool back then too. You showed me your rough drafts and asked calmly."
"My mother said to always keep the drafts."
"She's right. Keep doing that."
Uma walked out lighter. At lunch, when her friends asked what sir wanted, she just said, "He fixed my marks." She didn't add anything else.

qa.q: Where did Thomas sir find Uma's second map?
What was Uma feeling when Thomas sir apologised?
qa.a: She felt vindicated and was tempted to gloat, wanting to say she had told him so.

qa.q: What did Uma do well, and what lesson does she keep?
qa.a: She accepted the apology graciously and didn't boast to friends, keeping the lesson to save drafts and raise concerns calmly.

qa.q: How does Thomas sir see Uma's behaviour?
qa.a: He respects that she stayed calm and kept evidence, and he encourages her to keep doing it.

grounding: A teen whose teacher admits a marking error feels vindicated but accepts it graciously and keeps the lesson about raising concerns.
